name: literature
code_version_note: the commit at build time, which precedes the commit that lands this file
method: Four query families over PubMed E-utilities: <gene> AND (repurposing OR inhibitor OR <anchor>); <pathway head phrase> AND drug; per direction, the direction name with its slash-separated segments OR'd, AND <anchor>; and the PMIDs the card itself cites. <anchor> is the last alphabetic word of the card's disease name. The direction family is the weak one: a long descriptive name becomes a long AND-chain and can match nothing. Those zeros are recorded in snapshot.json rather than papered over with a looser query.

inputs.name: pubmed
inputs.role: the literature behind the gene, the pathway and each direction
inputs.sha256_scope: roll-up: sha256 over the sorted sha256 digests of every cached reply body this build read from this API. A public API has no single byte stream to hash; this value is reproducible from the cache and changes when any reply changes.
queries: BUB1B AND (repurposing OR inhibitor OR aneuploidy)
(SAC reinforcement OR chromosomal-instability reduction) AND aneuploidy
(proteostasis OR BubR1 stabilisation for a hypomorph) AND aneuploidy
(cancer prevention in the MVA1 tumour context) AND aneuploidy
inputs.known_gap: this API states no release or version in its replies, so the field is null rather than a date copied from the run.

licence: Every row is derived from a public API: Open Targets Platform (CC0), ChEMBL (CC BY-SA 3.0), DGIdb (MIT, aggregating sources under their own terms), Reactome (CC0), ClinicalTrials.gov (US public domain), PubMed/NCBI (US public domain) and openFDA (US public domain). No licensed resource is queried; DrugBank is named by the challenge form but requires a licence for programmatic access and was not used.
patient_data: none. Public API replies only - gene symbols, drug names, trial ids and citations. Nothing here was derived from the callset, and no genomic position appears in any row by construction.
